case_name: Sow Rinku Sujit Jamadar And Another vs Sujit Anant Jamadar

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Sow Rinku Sujit Jamadar And Another (wife)

facts_of_case: The parties were married in 2023 and had a one-year-old child. The wife filed for divorce and the husband also sought dissolution of marriage. Both parties filed multiple applications.

legal_principles.principle: The distance between the paternal village of the applicant and the place where the proceedings are being held can be a relevant factor in considering the convenience of the applicant.
legal_principles.held: Considering the law laid down in the case of N.C.V. Aishwarya V. A. S. Saravana Karthik Sha (Civil Appeal No.4894/2022), order dated 18.07.2022, passed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court, I
cited_cases: N.C.V. Aishwarya V. A. S. Saravana Karthik Sha (Civil Appeal No.4894/2022)

legal_principles.principle: A lactating mother may face inconvenience in travelling with her one-year-old baby, especially if the distance is significant.

outcome.final_order: H.M.P. No.167 of 2024 was withdrawn from the file of learned Civil Judge, Senior Division, Jaisingpur and transferred to the file of Family Court at Latur.
